525	So Rav Shach, on Purim, a few students from the yeshiva came to him.
526	They sat with him, words of Torah, and there was joy.
527	Suddenly Rabbi Shlomo Lorincz walked in.
528	Do you remember him?

531	Head of the Finance Committee.
532	Head of the Finance Committee.
533	He walked in, and the students immediately understood: Rabbi Lorincz came in, a Knesset member, so they had to
534	give up their seats, in any case, a distinguished person, came in.
535	So they stood up and came to clear the place for him to enter. He came with a mishloach manot.
536	Rav Shach signaled to them, sit down.
537	He took Rabbi Lorincz to the kitchen.
538	He gave him a different mishloach manot, accompanied him outside, did everything fully.
539	He came back and told them: as important as he is, and as much as he brings merit to the many, and much depends on him.

544	And therefore the Gemara says in Tractate Megillah, page 16b:
545	Torah study is greater than saving lives. What does it mean that Torah study is greater
546	than saving lives?
547	The Atei Zahav says, Yoreh De'ah, siman 251, subsection 6, Laws of Tzedakah:
548	Suppose there is now some suicide terrorist, may HaShem have mercy, who wants to enter
549	the mall there, Malha Mall.
550	He wants to enter the mall and carry out an attack, and the security guard discovers it, immediately pounces
551	on him, takes him down to the floor, ties his hands. Let's bring a story, yes.
552	Okay, and he saved all the people in Malha Mall. They will let him light
553	a torch on Independence Day, and he will receive a citizen's, I don't know how to say it, some
554	medal of honor. But a yeshiva student, or a person who sits here and learns
